کمتر از دو هفته مانده به انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای آمریکا، نظرسنجی‌ها از شرایط نه‌چندان مطلوب دونالد ترامپ حکایت دارند. میزان رضایت از عملکرد او، چه در حوزه اقتصاد و چه در مدیریت جنگ با ایران، به پایین‌ترین سطح خود در دو سال گذشته رسیده است. رئیس‌جمهور هشتادساله آمریکا در تلاش برای افزایش شانس پیروزی نامزدهای حزبش، سفرهای فشرده‌ای به ایالت‌های مختلف انجام می‌دهد و در گردهمایی‌های انتخاباتی سخنرانی‌های طولانی ایراد می‌کند.

با این حال، بخش قابل توجهی از رسانه‌های آمریکایی همچنان تمرکز خود را بر جنگ ایران و پیامدهای آن برای سیاست خارجی ایالات متحده، جایگاه این کشور در نظام بین‌الملل و درس‌هایی که این جنگ درباره تعریف دوباره قدرت نظامی آمریکا و محدودیت‌های آن به همراه داشته، حفظ کرده‌اند.

در این میان مجله آتلانتیک از بروز شکاف‌هایی در نزدیک‌ترین حلقه سیاسی و خانوادگی ترامپ خبر داده است. این نشریه به نقل از دو منبع آگاه گزارش داده که دونالد ترامپ جونیور، پسر بزرگ رئیس‌جمهور، از همان آغاز با ورود آمریکا به جنگ با ایران مخالف بوده و مخالفت خود را در گفت‌وگوهای خصوصی و خانوادگی به پدرش نیز منتقل کرده است.

آتلانتیک می‌نویسد ترامپ جونیور که از چهره‌های نزدیک به جریان «اول آمریکا» محسوب می‌شود، سال‌ها نسبت به مداخلات نظامی آمریکا در خارج از کشور بدبین بوده و معتقد است واشنگتن نباید وارد جنگی تازه در خاورمیانه می‌شد.

این گزارش، مخالفت ترامپ جونیور را نشانه‌ای از شکافی عمیق‌تر در اردوگاه «ماگا» می‌داند؛ شکافی میان ملی‌گرایان حامی رئیس‌جمهور که مداخله در جنگ‌های خارجی را در تضاد با شعار «اول آمریکا» می‌بینند و چهره‌های تندروتری که خواهان برخوردی سخت‌گیرانه‌تر با کشورهایی مانند ایران هستند. همزمان، برخی نامزدهای جمهوری‌خواه نیز در کارزارهای انتخاباتی خود مواضعی انتقادی‌تر نسبت به جنگ با ایران اتخاذ کرده‌اند، هرچند این رویکرد را نمی‌توان به همه نامزدهای این حزب تعمیم داد.

منبع تصویر، Anadolu via Getty Images

روزنامه وال استریت ژورنال با گزارشی از کنفرانس امنیتی دوحه، تصویری از ژئوپولتیک منطقه پس از جنگ ایران ترسیم می‌کند که در آن دولت‌های عرب خلیج فارس باید سهم بیشتری از هزینه انسانی، مالی و سیاسی امنیت خود را بر عهده بگیرند. منطقه‌ای که  از چتر امنیتی آمریکا مانند گذشته برخوردار نخواهند بود.

این روزنامه با نقل گفته‌های تام باراک، سفیر آمریکا در ترکیه و نماینده ویژه آقای ترامپ برای سوریه و عراق، از هشدار او به کشورهای منطقه در جریان مجمع جهانی امنیت در دوحه نوشته است. بر این اساس آقای باراک گفته است «ترتیبات پس از جنگ جهانی دوم، یعنی نوعی معامله متقابل که بر اساس آن آمریکا امنیت را تأمین می‌کرد و در مقابل به نفت دسترسی داشت، دیگر با اولویت‌های واشنگتن همخوانی ندارند.»

به گفته او، آمریکایی‌ها دیگر نمی‌خواهند جان خود را برای خاورمیانه به خطر بیندازند و کشورهای حاشیه خلیج فارس نیز می‌دانند که آمریکا نمی‌تواند امنیت آن‌ها را به طور کامل تضمین کند.

وال‌استریت ژورنال می‌نویسد کشورهای حاشیه خلیج فارس با نگرانی تحولات عربستان سعودی را زیر نظر دارند؛ جایی که حملات موشکی و پهپادی حوثی‌های مورد حمایت ایران، تأسیسات انرژی و فرودگاه بین‌المللی ریاض را هدف قرار داده است. به نوشته این روزنامه، درخواست‌های مکرر ریاض برای دریافت حمایت نظامی از آمریکا نیز نتیجه‌ای در پی نداشته و واشنگتن کمک‌های خود را عمدتاً به اشتراک‌گذاری اطلاعات و پشتیبانی اطلاعاتی محدود کرده است.

زمان‌بندی این هشدار نیز معنادار به نظر می‌رسد. در حالی که فشار محاصره دریایی آمریکا علیه ایران ادامه دارد و نشانه‌هایی از احتمال بازگشت طرف‌های درگیر به میدان نبرد دیده می‌شود، واشنگتن آشکارا به کشورهای منطقه پیام می‌دهد که دوران اتکای کامل به چتر امنیتی آمریکا رو به پایان است؛ کشورهایی که به تعبیر مقام‌های آمریکایی، باید مانند «نوجوانانی» بیاموزند با اتکای بیشتر به خود از امنیتشان دفاع کنند.

منبع تصویر، AFP via Getty Images

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

مقاله‌ای  درباره درس‌های جنگ با ایران در نشریه فارین افرز منتشر شده که  به قلم یکی از شناخته‌شده‌ترین فرماندهان نظامی معاصر آمریکا، ویلیام مک ریون، دریادار چهارستاره‌ آمریکایی و فرمانده پیشین نیروهای عملیات ویژه این کشور است. آقای مک ریون اگرچه با سخنرانی و کتابی با عنوان «تختت را مرتب کن» شهرت جهانی یافت اما شهرت اصلی‌ او در دنیای جنگ بیش از هر چیز به دلیل طراحی و نظارت بر عملیات کشتن اسامه بن‌لادن در پاکستان در سال ۲۰۱۱ است.

او در مقاله خود که عنوان آن «محدودیت‌های قدرت آمریکا، استراتژی و توهم زور» (استفاده از نیروی نظامی) است جنگ ایران را  صرفاً خطای دولت ترامپ نمی‌داند، بلکه نمونه‌ای از محدودیت‌های ذاتی قدرت نظامی آمریکا و جلوه‌ای تازه از یک بیماری دیرپا در سیاست خارجی این کشور خوانده است: ایمانی مبالغه‌آمیز به اینکه توان نظامی می‌تواند مسائل ذاتاً سیاسی را حل کند. او هشدار می‌دهد که برتری نظامی به معنای توانایی دستیابی به هر هدف سیاسی نیست و تجربه‌های تاریخی نشان داده‌اند که مشروعیت اخلاقی یک جنگ و توانایی متقاعد کردن افکار عمومی و متحدان، نقشی تعیین‌کننده در سرنوشت  جنگ‌ها دارند.

اما هسته اصلی استدلال او بر فهرستی از محدودیت‌های قدرت آمریکا استوار است؛ محدودیت‌هایی که در جنگ با ایران نیز بار دیگر خود را نشان دادند: مشروعیت اخلاقی، جغرافیا، اراده دشمن، بی‌میلی به اعزام نیروی زمینی، عامل زمان و کیفیت رهبری. او می‌نویسد در هر جامعه‌ای «غول خفته‌ای» وجود دارد که در برابر حمله خارجی، با انگیزه دفاع از حقانیت یا بقا بیدار می‌شود؛ واقعیتی که به اعتقاد او آمریکا این بار نیز، همانند جنگ‌های عراق و افغانستان، از درک آن بازمانده است. از نگاه او، تنگه هرمز همچنان «برگ برنده» ایران محسوب می‌شود؛ یک مانع ژئوپلیتیک که حتی برتری هوایی و دریایی آمریکا نیز به آسانی قادر به بی‌اثر کردن آن نیست.

آقای مک‌ریون در نهایت هشدار داده است که بدون رهبری سیاسی و نظامی کارآمد، اهداف روشن، ائتلاف‌سازی مؤثر و تعریف واقع‌بینانه از پیروزی، حتی قدرتمندترین ارتش جهان نیز نمی‌تواند به نتایج مطلوب دست پیدا کند.

بسیاری از همین نگرانی‌ها، از هزینه و دوام جنگ تا هدف نهایی و اثرش بر قیمت انرژی و زندگی آمریکا‌یی‌ها به‌نوعی   ذهن رأی‌دهندگانی را مشغول کرده  که به‌زودی پای صندوق‌های رأی می‌روند.

نارضایتی گسترده از نحوه مدیریت جنگ و افزایش نگرانی از اقتصاد و هزینه‌های انرژی یک بار دیگرسیاست خارجی را به زندگی روزمره آمریکایی‌ها  پیوند زده است. انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای می‌تواند  نشان دهد که رأی‌دهندگان تا چه حد پشت سر رهبران خود در جنگ با ایران می‌ایستند.

اما هسته اصلی استدلال او بر فهرستی از محدودیت‌های قدرت آمریکا استوار است؛ محدودیت‌هایی که در جنگ با ایران نیز بار دیگر خود را نشان دادند: مشروعیت اخلاقی، جغرافیا، اراده دشمن، بی‌میلی به اعزام نیروی زمینی، عامل زمان و کیفیت رهبری. او می‌نویسد در هر جامعه‌ای «غول خفته‌ای» وجود دارد که در برابر حمله خارجی، با انگیزه دفاع از حقانیت یا بقا بیدار می‌شود؛ واقعیتی که به اعتقاد او آمریکا این بار نیز، همانند جنگ‌های عراق و افغانستان، از درک آن بازمانده است. از نگاه او، تنگه هرمز همچنان «برگ برنده» ایران محسوب می‌شود؛ یک مانع ژئوپلیتیک که حتی برتری هوایی و دریایی آمریکا نیز به آسانی قادر به بی‌اثر کردن آن نیست.

آقای مک‌ریون در نهایت هشدار داده است که بدون رهبری سیاسی و نظامی کارآمد، اهداف روشن، ائتلاف‌سازی مؤثر و تعریف واقع‌بینانه از پیروزی، حتی قدرتمندترین ارتش جهان نیز نمی‌تواند به نتایج مطلوب دست پیدا کند.

بسیاری از همین نگرانی‌ها، از هزینه و دوام جنگ تا هدف نهایی و اثرش بر قیمت انرژی و زندگی آمریکا‌یی‌ها به‌نوعی   ذهن رأی‌دهندگانی را مشغول کرده  که به‌زودی پای صندوق‌های رأی می‌روند.

نارضایتی گسترده از نحوه مدیریت جنگ و افزایش نگرانی از اقتصاد و هزینه‌های انرژی یک بار دیگرسیاست خارجی را به زندگی روزمره آمریکایی‌ها  پیوند زده است. انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای می‌تواند  نشان دهد که رأی‌دهندگان تا چه حد پشت سر رهبران خود در جنگ با ایران می‌ایستند.

The State Department imposed sanctions on Beijing-based MiraclePlus and four related entities Monday over the
news.originalContent:
Photo by Paul Faith / AFP via Getty Images

A Chinese firm that bankrolled a convicted Google artificial intelligence thief grew out of a program launched by Sam Altman.

The State Department imposed sanctions on Beijing-based MiraclePlus and four related entities Monday over their ties to former Google engineer Linwei Ding, who was convicted of stealing the company’s AI trade secrets in January, according to a department statement. MiraclePlus traces back to a Chinese program that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman launched while running Y Combinator in 2018, Bloomberg reported.

Ding founded Shanghai Zhisuan Technology, which is among those sanctioned by the department, in 2023, and later sought funding from MiraclePlus in his application into its program, the department stated. (EXCLUSIVE: Big Ten School Joined Forces With Chinese University On Car-Tracking Tech, Report Finds)

Ding was “touting his experience with and knowledge of Google’s technology and internal systems and claimed that Zhisuan could replicate Google’s SI infrastructure technology,” the department stated.

MiraclePlus accepted Ding into its program in Aug. 2023 and invested about $700,000 in exchange for a small ownership stake in the company, according to an Aug. 20 federal court order.

Lu Qi, a former Microsoft and Baidu executive whom Altman hired to run YC China, formed MiraclePlus with the program’s former team after Y Combinator shut it down in 2019, TechCrunch reported.

Lu was not among those sanctioned Monday, according to the department’s fact sheet.

”I am delighted to announce that Qi Lu is joining YC to launch and run YC China. I have been trying to recruit Qi for many years — he is one of the most impressive technologists I know,” Altman wrote in an Aug. 14 blog post for Y Combinator.

“Y Combinator has no affiliation with MiraclePlus or Lu Qi,” a Y Combinator spokesperson told the Daily Caller News Foundation.

Altman stepped down as Y Combinator’s president in 2019 to focus on OpenAI, Axios reported.

The State Department, MiraclePlus and OpenAI each did not respond to the DCNF’s requests for comment.

A federal jury found Ding guilty on seven charges of economic espionage and seven more charges for trade secret theft, the Justice Department announced on Jan. 29. Ding had stolen more than 2,000 confidential pages of Google AI files, which he allegedly placed in a personal cloud account to help China.

Ding was acquitted on the espionage charges on Aug. 20 due to lack of evidence that he took the files for the Chinese government, but his seven theft-of-trade secrets convictions remained, according to the federal court order.

“This theft of trade secrets is a serious threat to U.S. economic, foreign policy, and national security interests,” State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a Monday press statement.

news.originalContent:
Photo by Mark Wilson/Getty Images

Two of America’s largest defense contractors reported record order backlogs Tuesday, with RTX securing nearly $23 billion in Tomahawk cruise missile contracts as the Pentagon faced mounting costs to replace weapons expended during the war with Iran.

RTX disclosed a record $340 billion companywide backlog, including $164 billion in defense orders, while Northrop Grumman reported a record $109.6 billion in outstanding contracts. Although neither company attributed its overall backlog to the Iran conflict, RTX secured major orders for Tomahawk missiles and missile defense interceptors, weapons the U.S. military expended during the fighting.

RTX reported quarterly revenue climbed 11% to nearly $25 billion, according to its earnings release. Its Raytheon defense division generated $8 billion in sales, a 14% increase from a year earlier, driven by higher production volumes on naval weapons, Patriot air defense systems, Standard Missiles and Tomahawk cruise missiles.

Raytheon’s operating profit jumped 32% to $1.13 billion, while RTX secured more than $81 billion in new commercial aerospace and defense awards during the quarter.

RTX CEO Chris Calio said approximately $23 billion in Tomahawk contracts and more than $14 billion in AMRAAM missile orders accounted for the majority of the company’s nearly $59 billion in quarterly defense bookings. The Tomahawk orders included a $22.9 billion contract awarded in August to expand production for the U.S. Navy.

Northrop Grumman reported third-quarter revenue increased 7% to $11.1 billion, with its Aeronautics Systems division recording 14% growth and Defense Systems sales climbing 12%, according to its financial results.

The company secured $16.4 billion in new contracts during the quarter, including $2 billion for the Sentinel nuclear missile program, $1.4 billion for Virginia-class submarines and $1.3 billion for F-35 fighter aircraft. Those awards reflected broader military spending rather than contracts specifically identified as replacements for weapons used in Iran.

Northrop’s backlog increased 15% from the end of 2025, reaching $109.6 billion. Company filings showed approximately $50.1 billion of those orders were funded, while another $59.5 billion remained unfunded, illustrating how large contract backlogs do not necessarily translate into immediately available defense equipment.

The expanding defense business comes as American military operations in Iran have consumed substantial quantities of expensive weapons.

The Congressional Budget Office estimated that military operations against Iran cost approximately $38 billion through Aug. 1, including $21.7 billion to replace expended munitions. Of that amount, $13.1 billion involved missile defense interceptors, including Patriot, THAAD, SM-3 and SM-6 missiles, while another $7.3 billion involved land-attack cruise missiles, including Tomahawks. (RELATED: Iran War Costing Taxpayers Over $38,000,000,000 While They Struggle To Afford Basic Needs)

A July assessment from the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated American Patriot missile inventories had fallen below 1,000 interceptors, while Terminal High Altitude Area Defense inventories stood at approximately 250. Researchers warned that depleted stockpiles could threaten American military readiness in a potential confrontation with China.

RTX subsequently announced a contract worth up to $24.4 billion for SM-6 interceptors on Oct. 1, followed by another agreement worth up to $6.3 billion for SM-3 interceptors on Oct. 8. Raytheon said the SM-3 contract supported urgent replenishment of missile defense inventories used in combat, although it did not specifically attribute the orders to Iran. Both agreements were announced after the third quarter ended.

RTX also booked approximately $4.7 billion in Patriot interceptor orders for Ukraine and Poland during the second quarter, according to its filings. Lockheed Martin separately received a contract worth up to $35 billion in June to expand THAAD interceptor production.

Defense manufacturers have also begun pursuing substantial production increases. RTX announced agreements with the Pentagon in February designed to eventually raise annual production to more than 1,000 Tomahawk missiles, at least 1,900 AMRAAM air-to-air missiles and more than 500 SM-6 missiles.

Those figures represent production targets rather than current manufacturing output, meaning significant additional capacity will be necessary to fulfill the planned increases.

Even with increased manufacturing output, rebuilding depleted missile defense inventories would likely take at least five years, the CBO estimated, citing historically slow production expansion and delays between contract awards and weapons deliveries.

Northrop Grumman projected sales growth of 5% to 7% in 2027 as it expands production on major military programs. CEO Kathy Warden pointed to investments in manufacturing capacity as necessary to support future growth, while RTX executives identified supply chain constraints involving rocket motors, castings and circuit boards as obstacles to increasing production.

The Daily Caller News Foundation contacted RTX, Northrop Grumman and the Department of Defense for comment, but none responded.

news.originalTitle: Obama Admin Paid Americans To Scrap 680,000 Cars. Are Today’s Would-Be Car Buyers Suffering The Consequences?
news.title: Obama Admin Paid Americans To Scrap 680,000 Cars. Are Today’s Would-Be Car Buyers Suffering The Consequences?
news.originalSummary:
Former President Barack Obama’s administration paid Americans to destroy nearly 680,000 functioning vehicles in 2009, permanently removing cars from the road as today’s buyers confront a shrinking supply of affordable transportation and mounting auto debt.

The $2.85 billion Cash for Clunkers program offered motorists thousands of dollars toward new vehicles in exchange for surrendering older cars
news.summary:
Former President Barack Obama’s administration paid Americans to destroy nearly 680,000 functioning vehicles in 2009, permanently removing cars from the road as today’s buyers confront a shrinking supply of affordable transportation and mounting auto debt.

The $2.85 billion Cash
news.originalContent:
Former President Barack Obama’s administration paid Americans to destroy nearly 680,000 functioning vehicles in 2009, permanently removing cars from the road as today’s buyers confront a shrinking supply of affordable transportation and mounting auto debt.

The $2.85 billion Cash for Clunkers program offered motorists thousands of dollars toward new vehicles in exchange for surrendering older cars and trucks for destruction. While the initiative helped boost automobile sales during the Great Recession, it also eliminated drivable vehicles that could have provided affordable transportation for budget-conscious buyers.

Affordable used vehicles are becoming particularly scarce. Cars priced below $15,000 accounted for just 15.7% of used-vehicle dealership inventory in September, down from 19.4% a year earlier, according to a Friday report from Cox Automotive. Inventory in that price category declined 16.2% year over year, even as overall used-vehicle inventory increased.

The average used-vehicle listing price reached $27,235 in September, its highest level since December 2022, according to Cox Automotive. Meanwhile, monthly payments averaged $765 for new vehicles and $542 for used vehicles during the second quarter of 2026, according to Experian. (RELATED: More Americans Turning To Skyrocketing Car Loan Payments Just To Afford Vehicle)

Obama signed the Consumer Assistance to Recycle and Save Act in June 2009, establishing a program that provided buyers with $3,500 or $4,500 toward more fuel-efficient vehicles. To qualify, trade-ins had to be drivable and continuously insured and registered for at least a year. Dealerships were required to disable their engines before sending them to facilities for crushing or shredding, according to the Government Accountability Office’s review.

Approximately 85% of the vehicles surrendered were trucks, SUVs or other qualifying light trucks, many of which remained operational when they entered the program. Their mandatory destruction prevented those vehicles from being resold as inexpensive transportation, removing potential options for first-time buyers and lower-income Americans unable to afford new cars.

Used-car dealership representatives told the GAO that prices for vehicles at least ten years old increased during the program. However, they cautioned that the recession was also constraining used-vehicle supplies, making the program’s independent effect difficult to determine.

The destruction also restricted the availability of replacement parts. Federal rules prohibited the resale of engines and assembled drivetrains, which salvage industry representatives told the GAO typically accounted for 60% to 65% of a salvaged vehicle’s value. The Specialty Equipment Market Association warned that the program threatened auto restorers, repair shops and hobbyists who relied on older vehicles for replacement components. Other parts could be salvaged, and vehicles at least 25 years old were exempted from the program.

Research also questioned the initiative’s broader economic benefits. Economists Atif Mian and Amir Sufi found that Cash for Clunkers generated approximately 360,000 additional vehicle purchases during July and August 2009, but almost all of those purchases were offset by reduced buying in subsequent months.

The program did improve fuel efficiency among participating vehicles. Government auditors reported that replacement vehicles averaged 24.9 miles per gallon, compared with 15.7 miles per gallon for vehicles traded in.

The extent to which the 2009 program contributed to today’s used-car shortages remains uncertain. Cox Automotive reported in July that reduced vehicle production and sales during the COVID-19 pandemic continued to constrain supplies of four- to six-year-old used cars, illustrating more recent pressures on the market.

Meanwhile, outstanding American auto debt reached $1.713 trillion during the second quarter of 2026, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Its report showed the annualized share of auto-loan balances entering serious delinquency rose to 3.00%, compared with 2.93% a year earlier.

news.originalContent:
Photo by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images

Gen Z and millennial customers recorded the fastest growth in credit card spending at Synchrony Financial during the third quarter, the company reported Tuesday, as rising living expenses and elevated borrowing costs strained household budgets.

The lender’s purchase volume climbed 8% to $49.7 billion, with younger consumers driving the strongest growth. The spending increase coincided with mounting affordability pressures, as Federal Reserve research found nearly half of Americans under 30 received financial assistance with expenses in 2025.

Synchrony CEO Brian Doubles said spending increased across generations and credit categories, with the fastest growth among younger customers. The company reported double-digit growth in spending outside its retail partners on both essential and discretionary purchases, including gas stations, electronics and discount stores.

Higher prices themselves contributed to the increase. Synchrony attributed part of its 9% purchase-volume growth in its Home & Auto division and 13% growth in its Diversified & Value division to rising gasoline prices, illustrating how consumers can spend more without necessarily purchasing more goods.

The financial pressures facing younger Americans extend beyond credit cards. A Federal Reserve survey released in May found 47% of adults ages 18 to 29 received help from someone outside their household to cover expenses in 2025, including housing, utilities, transportation and everyday purchases.

The same research found 49% of adults under 30 lived with a parent, up 12 percentage points from 2019. Nearly one-quarter of Americans ages 18 to 29 failed to pay all their bills in full during the month preceding the survey.

Housing affordability compounded the challenge. Home prices increased 54% nationally since 2020, according to Harvard University’s Joint Center for Housing Studies, while nearly half of renter households spent more than 30% of their income on housing at the latest count.

The pressure intensified in September as consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier, while inflation-adjusted average hourly earnings fell 0.7%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. (RELATED: Americans’ Wage Gains Wiped Out By Inflation For 5 Straight Months As Iran War Fallout Continued)

Federal Reserve data also revealed a widening divide between financially comfortable Americans and those struggling to make ends meet. Average credit card balances among respondents who reported difficulty getting by increased 37%, or $2,530, between 2023 and 2025. Balances among those living comfortably increased just 1%, or $59.

Carrying that debt remains expensive. The average interest rate on credit card accounts assessed interest reached 22.36% in August, according to Federal Reserve data. The Fed’s household survey found 46% of credit card holders ages 18 to 29 carried a balance at least once during 2025.

Synchrony’s outstanding loans increased 3% to $103.3 billion in the third quarter, although its delinquency figures offered a more encouraging picture. Loans at least 30 days past due declined to 4.34% from 4.39% a year earlier, while loans at least 90 days past due fell to 2.06% from 2.12%.

news.originalContent: The IDF addressed the strikes carried out overnight in southern Lebanon, including in the village of Kfar Reman, saying on Monday afternoon that they began after Hezbollah terrorists launched two explosive drones at Israeli forces on the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon. No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility.   No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility. A vehicle in which two people were killed. The Associated Press reported that the vehicle belonged to the Lebanese Scout and Rescue Association, Al-Risala, and that one of those killed was a paramedic with the organization. Two other people were wounded. At the same time, Lebanese reports said a building in Kfar Reman where a large number of people were staying was also struck, killing nine people, including women and children, and wounding 11 others.   Prior to the strikes, steps were taken to mitigate harm to uninvolved individuals, including the use of precise munitions and aerial surveillance," the IDF said in response. "The claim that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strikes is being reviewed.” The IDF said that, in addition, following the launch of the explosive drones Sunday, “the IDF struck in the Nabatieh area and eliminated several Hezbollah terrorists. "The IDF will not allow the Hezbollah terrorist organization to harm Israeli civilians or IDF soldiers and will continue to operate to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement." “We lived under constant intimidation because of the bombardments on the outskirts of the village,” Fouad Chakroun, a resident of Kfar Reman told AP as he stood in front of the destroyed building. “Now they have struck the heart of the village.” Another resident, Saleh Madlij, said families and children had been staying in the building. “Are there missiles here?” he said sarcastically. “I will not leave this place.” The BBC reported that, according to Lebanese media, seven additional people were killed in strikes Sunday, while Lebanese President Joseph Aoun warned that the attacks represented a “dangerous escalation” that threatened the ceasefire.

According to them, the situation only worsens, and the support the world has shown Israel following Hamas’s attack on October 7 has already been forgotten. Ministers in the government blame Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the complete neglect of Israel’s public relations: "There’s no leader present it’s been abandoned. A pandemic of sanctions against Israel may break out, and if we don't wake up, it will be too late. Something big needed to be done in terms of public relations, we need to rally the Jewish people and launch an international campaign. There’s no leader to head this. We’re losing. Our friends tell us: we support you, but you’re losing in the court of public opinion." A senior figure in Israel's advocacy efforts added, "They neutralized the Foreign Ministry and took away all its budget. The Foreign Ministry has no funding. To this day, no money was delivered. We’re working with a budget of 2 million shekels allocated for the war since the beginning of the year.  “Each U.S. consulate receives $5,000 a year for public relations efforts, including Independence Day events. For example, the consulate in Boston, which is also responsible for MIT, has to struggle to have such an amount. It’s ridiculous. When you already have a talented spokesman like Eylon Levy, they unjustly suspend him. He was one of the few people who did his mission in the most talented, beautiful, and correct way, and they sent him home,” the source said.   Internal reports from Israeli missions in the United States describe a very harsh picture of Israeli coverage in the American media. One report described, "The media awaited a sign from the government for a policy change, and when it arrived - it unleashed a rampage and published constant harsh criticism against Israel that had always existed. The harsh reports from Gaza, alongside internal tensions in the U.S., threaten to push moderate writers from the mainstream to adopt critical positions toward Israel and demand an immediate and permanent cease-fire.” 'the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy' “Pressure on the Biden administration to harden its stance toward Israel and condition military aid for an Israeli policy change constitutes a warning sign for the future,” the report added. “In terms of 'color,' we’re currently in a 'dark orange.' “There’s a change in stances even among staunch supporters of Israel – and while the conservative media fully supported Israel's actions in the past, this time voices questioning the proportionality of Israeli action have also been heard. However, no demand for a cease-fire is expected to appear in those media outlets. Without a fundamental change in the humanitarian issue in Gaza and/or signs on the diplomatic solution on the horizon, criticism of Israel in the media is expected to intensify,” the report read. It was added, "In the last month, the U.S. media’s spotlight turned to the worsening humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with special emphasis given to the suffering of Rafah residents against the backdrop of the possibility of the IDF expanding the ground operation there as well. Leading media outlets flooded screens and front pages with images of starving children, trauma victims, and the destruction of homes and hospitals. Reports and personal stories from Rafah led to empathy toward the Palestinians’ suffering and anger toward Israel's military actions. "Although most media outlets refrained from blaming Israel for creating the crisis intentionally or denying its right to self-defense, opinion pieces sparked fierce debate regarding the proportionality and morality of the ongoing military operation in its current form. Critical voices that were once silenced now have a wider platform.    “Reports focused on the immense humanitarian damages and the harm to innocent civilians, which many analysts argue is unjustified and goes against the values of the IDF’s operation. Even publicists who supported Israel in the past admitted that the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy,” the report read. “Against this backdrop, a narrative is emerging among liberal authors, which sees the Biden administration and its policy of providing weapons and diplomatic support to Israel as responsible for the situation, or at least as someone who can bring it to an end." Furthermore, dozens of recent opinion pieces represent a wide range of positions regarding the IDF’s legitimacy, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, the question of a cease-fire, and the future of U.S.-Israel relations: Conservative media outlets like The Wall Street Journal and The New York Post fully support Israel, advocate for continued military action against Hamas, and refrain from calling for an immediate and prolonged stop to the war.  In contrast, newspapers identified with the center and liberal left, including The New York Times and The Washington Post, criticize the war’s escalation, citing the destructive consequences of the confrontation on Palestinian civilians, and therefore calling for an immediate humanitarian cease-fire, the reports explained.   The reports also expose an erosion of Israel's standing in Washington against the backdrop of the escalation in the Gaza war. This was clearly reflected in U.S. President Joe Biden's statement regarding a "red line" on military operations in Rafah, and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech.  Most analysts don’t foresee an immediate shift in relations between the countries, but caution against potential political damage to both sides. Furthermore, calls are increasing to use American military aid to Israel as leverage to force policy change in Jerusalem. However, warnings have been raised that the fact of having this discussion could bolster Hamas's position and undermine the chances of a cease-fire.  While conservative media outlets present Israel's policy as legitimate self-defense, liberal media outlets provide a platform for writers who echo the Palestinian narrative, sometimes using rhetoric accusing Israel of "apartheid" and even "genocide." Calls for the U.S. government to distance itself from supporting Israel and reconsider its military aid plan are becoming more common, even in moderate media outlets. The report mentions articles in The Washington Post and The Daily Beast highlighting the effectiveness of pro-Palestinian activists in influencing public opinion in the U.S., especially among progressive Democratic voters. The articles point to growing discontent with the Biden administration's support for Israel, reflected in "Uncommitted" votes in the Democratic primaries and disruptions at party events. Tactics such as demanding a cease-fire and using the term "genocide" have succeeded in keeping the war at the forefront of the national political agenda and increasing pressure on Washington to minimize its support of Israel.  The increasing willingness of Democratic politicians to criticize Israel suggests a shift in the party's traditional stance and leads to speech free of restraint in media outlets as well. This trend reached its zenith with Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech, in which he labeled Netanyahu an "obstacle to peace" and accused him of damaging Israel's international standing, calling for early Israeli elections.

news.title: 'We are in Shock': British Jews react to fatal terror attack - and fume at the 'lax response' of the UK
news.originalSummary: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities. news.originalContent: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities.   Follow Ynetnews on Facebook and Twitter >> Related stories: Israel names two sisters killed in West Bank terror attack At least one dead and six injured in a terror attack in Tel Aviv Family loses two daughters to deadly terror attack Members of the Jewish London community, including friends of the family, who heard of the devastating news after the Shabbat ended, were confronted only then, with the horrific reports of Maia and Rina's death. The funerals for the Dee sisters will be held today at the Kfar Etzion Cemetery.   Rabbi Leo Dee served as the Assistant Rabbi at the Hendon United Synagogue in North London from 2008-2011, and as the Senior Rabbi at Radlett United Synagogue from 2011-2014, after which the family made aliyah. They were a much beloved and respected family in the UK Jewish community. “People feel shock and disappointment. The family were communal people and served their communities well and were well-liked.” said a former member of the congregation at Hendon United Synagogue who did not wish to be named.  “I feel sick seeing this… good people who would never hurt anyone, murdered. I can't imagine his anguish, and pray Lucy survives,” said Joseph, another former congregant.   Chief UK Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis laments the death of the British-Israeli girls murdered in Friday's terror strike on the West Bank.  In a statement, the rabbi said: "No words can describe the depth of our shock and sadness at the heartbreaking news of the murder by terrorists in Israel of Maya & Rina Dee, daughters of Rebbetzen Lucy, who is in a critical condition & Rabbi Leo Dee, my dear colleagues. He continued, “They were much loved in the Hendon and Radlett communities in the UK, as well as in Israel and well beyond.” UK statement not mentioning terrorism The British Board of Deputies also issued a statement expressing shock over the tragic attack: “We are deeply shocked and saddened at the murder by Palestinian terrorists of Maia and Rina Dee, the daughters of Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee formerly of Radlett United Synagogue. We wish Lucy Refuah Shlemah and long life to the family as they cope with this devastating news.” Palestinian terrorist shot and killed 2 British-Israeli nationals, also critically injuring their mother in the West Bank. The victims were identified Saturday as 15-year-old Rina Dee and 20-year-old Maia Dee, the daughters of British-born Rabbi Leo Dee.  While their mother, Lucy (Lea), remains in critical condition fighting for her life, the Jewish community in the UK has expressed shock and sorrow at the brutal act of terrorism against former members of their community.    While many Jewish community leaders spoke out about the attack, the UK government has received criticism from some members of the community for its weakly-worded response to the killing of two of its own citizens.  One member of the Jewish community told Ynet that it was shocking that the UK statement didn’t even mention terrorism. “The response would be different if this happened elsewhere in the world. There is a double standard for British people killed in Israel,” he said.  The UK’s official statement read: “We are saddened to hear about the deaths of two British-Israeli citizens and the serious injuries sustained by a third individual. The UK calls for all parties across the region to de-escalate tensions.” "Tragedy for global Jewish community" Avi Abelow, family friend, said Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee are beloved and active members of their community in Efrat. "Two of the sweetest people with the sweetest children", he added. "Rabbi Leo continues to teach Torah classes in his Efrat synagogue today. All the youth of Efrat, as their families, are mourning the loss of either their personal friend or the sibling of their personal friend."  He mentioned that "Just last night the whole community got together, including many youth, for a special communal prayer gathering to pray for Lucy's recovery. The brutal Arab Muslim terrorist attack that murdered these two young, innocent Jewish women, and seriously injured their mother fighting for her life, is not just a tragedy for their family, but for the whole Efrat community and the global Jewish community.  "At the same time that another terrorist committed a terror attack in Tel Aviv, which killed an Italian tourist, and terrorist organizations are shooting rockets at Israel from Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, we are once again reminded that the Jewish people have enemies trying to kill us everywhere in our country for just being Jews living in our ancestral homeland.  "If only the UK government and other global bodies would recognize this truth, and truly give support to Israel to stop this ongoing terror war against Israel, which causes loss of life for everyone. In the meantime, as a personal friend and neighbor of the Dee family, my family, neighbors, and community will continue to assist and comfort the Dee family, as we assisted and comforted the family of our other friend and neighbor, Ari Fuld, murdered by terrorists back in 2018."
news.content: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities.   Follow Ynetnews on Facebook and Twitter >> Related stories: Israel names two sisters killed in West Bank terror attack At least one dead and six injured in a terror attack in Tel Aviv Family loses two daughters to deadly terror attack Members of the Jewish London community, including friends of the family, who heard of the devastating news after the Shabbat ended, were confronted only then, with the horrific reports of Maia and Rina's death. The funerals for the Dee sisters will be held today at the Kfar Etzion Cemetery.   Rabbi Leo Dee served as the Assistant Rabbi at the Hendon United Synagogue in North London from 2008-2011, and as the Senior Rabbi at Radlett United Synagogue from 2011-2014, after which the family made aliyah. They were a much beloved and respected family in the UK Jewish community. “People feel shock and disappointment. The family were communal people and served their communities well and were well-liked.” said a former member of the congregation at Hendon United Synagogue who did not wish to be named.  “I feel sick seeing this… good people who would never hurt anyone, murdered. I can't imagine his anguish, and pray Lucy survives,” said Joseph, another former congregant.   Chief UK Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis laments the death of the British-Israeli girls murdered in Friday's terror strike on the West Bank.  In a statement, the rabbi said: "No words can describe the depth of our shock and sadness at the heartbreaking news of the murder by terrorists in Israel of Maya & Rina Dee, daughters of Rebbetzen Lucy, who is in a critical condition & Rabbi Leo Dee, my dear colleagues. He continued, “They were much loved in the Hendon and Radlett communities in the UK, as well as in Israel and well beyond.” UK statement not mentioning terrorism The British Board of Deputies also issued a statement expressing shock over the tragic attack: “We are deeply shocked and saddened at the murder by Palestinian terrorists of Maia and Rina Dee, the daughters of Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee formerly of Radlett United Synagogue. We wish Lucy Refuah Shlemah and long life to the family as they cope with this devastating news.” Palestinian terrorist shot and killed 2 British-Israeli nationals, also critically injuring their mother in the West Bank. The victims were identified Saturday as 15-year-old Rina Dee and 20-year-old Maia Dee, the daughters of British-born Rabbi Leo Dee.  While their mother, Lucy (Lea), remains in critical condition fighting for her life, the Jewish community in the UK has expressed shock and sorrow at the brutal act of terrorism against former members of their community.    While many Jewish community leaders spoke out about the attack, the UK government has received criticism from some members of the community for its weakly-worded response to the killing of two of its own citizens.  One member of the Jewish community told Ynet that it was shocking that the UK statement didn’t even mention terrorism. “The response would be different if this happened elsewhere in the world. There is a double standard for British people killed in Israel,” he said.  The UK’s official statement read: “We are saddened to hear about the deaths of two British-Israeli citizens and the serious injuries sustained by a third individual. The UK calls for all parties across the region to de-escalate tensions.” "Tragedy for global Jewish community" Avi Abelow, family friend, said Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee are beloved and active members of their community in Efrat. "Two of the sweetest people with the sweetest children", he added. "Rabbi Leo continues to teach Torah classes in his Efrat synagogue today. All the youth of Efrat, as their families, are mourning the loss of either their personal friend or the sibling of their personal friend."  He mentioned that "Just last night the whole community got together, including many youth, for a special communal prayer gathering to pray for Lucy's recovery. The brutal Arab Muslim terrorist attack that murdered these two young, innocent Jewish women, and seriously injured their mother fighting for her life, is not just a tragedy for their family, but for the whole Efrat community and the global Jewish community.  "At the same time that another terrorist committed a terror attack in Tel Aviv, which killed an Italian tourist, and terrorist organizations are shooting rockets at Israel from Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, we are once again reminded that the Jewish people have enemies trying to kill us everywhere in our country for just being Jews living in our ancestral homeland.  "If only the UK government and other global bodies would recognize this truth, and truly give support to Israel to stop this ongoing terror war against Israel, which causes loss of life for everyone. In the meantime, as a personal friend and neighbor of the Dee family, my family, neighbors, and community will continue to assist and comfort the Dee family, as we assisted and comforted the family of our other friend and neighbor, Ari Fuld, murdered by terrorists back in 2018."
